title: A Generative AI-Based Framework for Decision Making in B2C E-Commerce: Conceptualization and Pilot Study
content: Decision making in business-to-consumer (B2C) e-commerce connects company and consumer activities before, during and after purchase. Existing generative artificial intelligence (GAI) applications usually address isolated tasks. This article develops a conceptual framework in which the five-stage Consumer Buying Behaviour (CBB) process structures GAI-assisted decisions. It links need clarification, information gathering, feasible-offer comparison, transaction review and post-purchase assessment in a recursive cycle with decision gates and bounded support functions. To illustrate its measurement and reporting procedure, five employees and three consumers completed baseline tasks followed by intended-to-be-comparable prompt-guided cases. No integrated GAI system, autonomous agent, live data connection or consequential transaction was implemented. The questionnaire items are descriptive indicators, not validated latent constructs, and findings are limited to participant-specific summaries. Several rubric-based and self-reported values were numerically more favourable in the second condition, but the fixed order prevents separation of prompt support from practice, familiarity, novelty, fatigue or expectancy effects. Technical accuracy, trust calibration, automation bias, commercial impact and post-purchase outcomes were not evaluated. The pilot is a procedural illustration and design input; it does not validate the framework or establish effectiveness. Larger randomized or counterbalanced studies using validated measures, task-level records and implemented-system tests are required.
